content:
Plan for Phase 68b at bcfdb56: docs/phases/cockpit-lanes-read-as-terminals.md. Front end only (cockpit.html/js/css + tests + docs); no server change planned.

The arbiter's brief: the lanes should emulate the terminal tabs — 'I want the lead window to show what I see in the lead tab… it's OK if it starts with a fresh output on each turn'; only the lead lane has a composer. The doc opens with a table of what the lanes are today, each row with the code it comes from.

Plan in five parts:
1. One turn = one terminal block in both lanes: a one-line header + the rendered turn log the server already streams, monospace, no inner max-height (today .act-lines is a 16em box inside a lane that also scrolls — nested scrollers). Newest block open, earlier blocks of the cycle folded; a running block is never folded. The LANE scrolls and follows only at the bottom, holding the reader's line with Phase 68's rowTopIn (not offsetTop) and a 'new output' cue. Stores / keys / SSE cursors (Phases 43/45/58) are kept: restyle and re-nest, not rewrite. Folded blocks hold no stream DOM; an open finished block is capped at 2,000 lines.
2. Both lanes scoped to the current cycle (the lead lane has no filter today → Phase 52 cards under the current header; open backlog item).
3. gate / panel / panel_lens items leave the reviewer's lane for a checks strip above the lanes; a chip opens that run's log.
4. One story: laneText stops deriving and shows n.headline.text for the headline's role; the lanes' 'gone' state and the Needs-you 'process disappeared — Cancel turn' card move from pid_alive === false to inflight.liveness === 'lost'; a new Needs-you card for headline states stalled / watcher-stale whose one action opens the Phase 68 drawer.
5. Tests: node harness for blocks/scoping/routing/liveness; a real-Chromium test for follow/hold with the shipped CSS; guards changed on purpose and listed; pid_alive joins the must-not-appear list for cockpit.js.

A BUG FOUND WHILE PLANNING, please check my reading: cockpit.js:578 shows the card '<agent>'s process disappeared mid-turn — Cancel turn' whenever n.inflight.pid_alive === false, and the lanes use the same test (995–1007). now_payload sets pid_alive False for pid None, which a gate marker has for its whole run and every cycle/panel marker has until its child is spawned — so a healthy 8-minute pre-check is shown as a lost process with a button that clears its record. Phase 68 fixed this for the headline only. I have READ this, not yet SEEN it; criterion 9 requires capturing it on a real pre-check before fixing it.

Three UX choices are marked as the arbiter's, with my recommendation (newest turn open + earlier folded; checks strip rather than a middle lane; a chat turn rendered as a turn block). He may interject.

Please look hardest at: whether 'restyle and re-nest' is realistic for fillMsgRow/renderLeadTimeline (the chat renderer is the one part I propose to replace); the performance caps; and whether part 4 belongs here or deserves its own small phase first, given the Cancel-turn card is a correctness problem and not a look.

Verified while planning: roadmap check ok; nothing implemented. Note: PR #54 (Phase 68c, tests only) is open and unmerged; this branch is cut from main and touches none of its files except docs/roadmap.md, which I will rebase.

Reviewed bcfdb56 and the existing lane/chat, headline, tail and SSE implementations. The proposed terminal blocks, checks strip and reuse of keyed stores are sound. Keep the owner-liveness correction in this phase: it directly supports the promised consistent status, and the diagnosis is correct (a missing child PID is not evidence that the owner is gone). No full-suite run is needed for this plan review. No arbiter interjections were present.

Please resolve two concrete gaps before implementation:

1. The unchanged watcher-off Needs-you card contradicts the headline for an already-delivered terminal turn. headline() deliberately says the agent has its turn and only the NEXT handoff is blocked when the watcher stops after delivery. renderNeeds currently says "Nothing runs ... until the watcher is on" for that same state. Scope section 4 explicitly retains this card unchanged, so "one story" would still be false. Make this card present the headline's delivered/undelivered distinction without re-deriving delivery in JS (using headline.text is sufficient), and add coverage for both cases. Preserve the distinction in the stale-watcher card too: a delivered agent may still be working even when dispatch monitoring stops.

2. Specify a realizable bounded log/reopen policy. There is no existing whole-log tail view: /api/tail returns JSON clamped to MAX_TAIL_LINES=2000, and cockpit.js explicitly says the old tail drawer is gone. Either scope the link honestly to the last 2,000 lines and offer the recorded local log path for the rest, or specify a concrete full-log mechanism using the existing SSE endpoint with its resource limits. Also make the caps explicit for running chat and cycle blocks, not only finished blocks: appendActLine already caps cycle output, whereas subscribeLead/LEAD.lines currently grows without a cap. Define what happens when trimming removes the reader's anchor. Add focused tests that folding drops stream DOM even if a final SSE line or delayed tail response arrives, and reopening does not duplicate or omit output. These are required consequences of the promised no-DOM folded blocks and preserved SSE cursors, not a request to rewrite the transport.

Implementation guidance (nonblocking): replacing fillMsgRow is realistic, but its existing signature includes streamed line count, so polling currently rebuilds the chat body. Preserve keyed stream DOM during the replacement and verify both chat and cycle hold/follow behavior in real Chromium, including cap rollover. Keep the recorded reply/error/continuity information when replacing the bubbles. The recommended UX choices can proceed unless the arbiter interjects.
